testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where are ABS malfunction lamps located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the air compressor must build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air once the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air once the air tanks reach 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to overheat and become less effective. This is called "fading."

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment when:
questions.explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially when they overheat from heavy use. Check brake adjustment frequently.

questions.question: Spring brakes activate when:

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a control on the dashboard is activated.
When the tires have minimal tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. When you see the low pressure warning signal, exit the road safely and stop the vehicle while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs approximately ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs approximately 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single air brake vehicle is:
questions.explanation: A single air brake vehicle should have a leakage rate no higher than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning signal:
questions.explanation: Test the low pressure warning light before every trip. After the system charges, rapidly apply and release the brake pedal to release air. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Where must the malfunction lamp be located on a dolly with ABS?
questions.explanation: A dolly with ABS must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common foundation brake.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil that build up in the system. If not removed, these can damage the brakes. Drains should be opened at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning signal goes off while driving?

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible
Stop where you are and park
Turn on hazard lights and continue driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates while driving, safely exit the road and park your vehicle as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Which one is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake is controlled by a knob. Pull the knob to apply the brakes. Push the knob in to release them.

questions.question: What happens when only the tractor has ABS?

options.text: The brakes work less effectively without ABS

questions.explanation: If only the tractor has ABS and the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing goes down. You should still be able to steer the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing out to one side.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks
How fast air is pumped into the tanks
The temperature of the air pumped into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
To allow for a change in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can build up and damage the brakes. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: To use stab braking in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
Push the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Push the brakes fully, lock the wheels, and keep holding the pedal down until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pushing the brakes fully until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling. Then repeat.

questions.question: Some air brake systems use alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
Oil parts of the brake system.
Stop rust from forming on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal on a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes a rod that moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal on a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out rods and moves slack adjusters. This twists the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes must have ABS if made on or after March 1, 1998.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This means two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system brakes different axles.
